title: Large-Scale Screening of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance Binding Interactions and Their Mixtures with Nuclear Receptors.
authors: Roy, Saptarshi; Moran, James; Danasekaran, Keerthana; O'Brien, Kate; Dakshanamurthy, Sivanesan
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接大规模筛选PFAS与核受体的正构和别构位点结合，虽属蛋白-配体互作而非TF-DNA体系，但对接与混合物建模方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Despite their significant impact, comprehensive screenings and detailed analyses of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) binding strengths at the orthosteric and allosteric sites of NRs are currently lacking. This study addresses this gap by focusing on the binding interaction analysis of both common and uncommon PFAS with the nuclear receptors (NRs) vitamin D receptor (VDR), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARgamma), pregnane X receptor (PXR), and estrogen receptor alpha (ERalpha). Advanced docking simulations were used to screen 9507 PFAS chemicals at the orthosteric and allosteric sites of PPARgamma, PXR, VDR, and ERalpha. All receptors exhibited strong binding interactions at the orthosteric and allosteric site with a significant number of PFAS. We verified the accuracy of the docking protocol through multiple docking controls and validations. A mixture modeling analysis indicates that PFAS can bind in various combinations with themselves and endogenous ligands simultaneously, to disrupt the endocrine system and cause carcinogenic responses. These findings reveal that PFAS can interfere with nuclear receptor activity by displacing endogenous or native ligands by binding to the orthosteric and allosteric sites. The purpose of this study is to explore the mechanisms through which PFAS exert their endocrine-disrupting effects, potentially leading to more targeted therapeutic strategies. Importantly, this study is the first to explore the binding of PFAS at allosteric sites and to model PFAS mixtures at nuclear receptors. Given the high concentration and persistence of PFAS in humans, this study further emphasizes the urgent need for further research into the carcinogenic mechanisms of PFAS and the development of therapeutic strategies that target nuclear receptors.
abstract_zh: 尽管全氟和多氟烷基物质（PFAS）具有显著影响，但目前缺乏对核受体（NRs）正构位点和变构位点上PFAS结合强度的全面筛选和详细分析。本研究通过聚焦常见及非常见PFAS与核受体（NRs）——维生素D受体（VDR）、过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ（PPARgamma）、孕烷X受体（PXR）和雌激素受体α（ERalpha）——的结合相互作用分析，填补了这一空白。采用先进的对接模拟技术，对9507种PFAS化学物质在PPARgamma、PXR、VDR和ERalpha的正构位点和变构位点进行了筛选。所有受体在正构位点和变构位点均表现出与大量PFAS的强结合相互作用。我们通过多重对接控制和验证确认了对接方案的准确性。混合物建模分析表明，PFAS可以以多种组合方式与自身及内源性配体同时结合，从而干扰内分泌系统并引发致癌反应。这些发现揭示，PFAS通过结合正构位点和变构位点，置换内源性或天然配体，从而干扰核受体活性。本研究旨在探索PFAS发挥其内分泌干扰效应的机制，可能为更具针对性的治疗策略提供依据。重要的是，本研究首次探索了PFAS在变构位点的结合，并对核受体上的PFAS混合物进行了建模。鉴于PFAS在人体中的高浓度和持久性，本研究进一步强调了迫切需要对PFAS致癌机制进行深入研究，并开发靶向核受体的治疗策略。
